title: budgeted-coldstart-prefetch-and-compact-quant-lib
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Customer workloads show an uneven arrival pattern causing expensive cold K/V cache misses and frequent cold-start token overhead for low-traffic tenants. This PR implements a budget-aware coldstart prefetch operator and ships a compact quantization profile library and a small CLI to generate tenant-level unit-econ presets. Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost for sparse tenants without regressing tail latency for high-throughput tenants. Scope: - Introduce a budgeted prefetch controller that enforces per-tenant coldstart budgets and selects a small set of seed KV prefixes to prefill based on recent arrival distribution. - Add tenant warmup profiles (sensible defaults) that are applied automatically when a tenant crosses an activity threshold; profiles are versioned and can be rolled back. - Ship a compact quant bundle format (.qbundle) containing pre-validated 4-bit and 8-bit calibration matrices for common decoder-only families; runtime picks the best compatible bundle using a checksum match. - Expose a small CLI (redwood econ-init) to synthesize unit-econ presets by sampling traces or using dry-run simulator outputs. Design decisions: - Prefetch strategy prioritizes prefix coverage over token depth for cold starts to maximize cache hits with limited budget. - Budget is expressed in microcredits per minute (configurable per tenant); controller will prefer cheaper prefill choices when budgets are tight. - Quant bundles are immutable artifacts stored in model registry; validating metadata includes expected input length distributions and kernel compatibility. - Default warmup profile is conservative (small prefetch set + slow ramp) to avoid sudden capacity spikes. Checklist: - [x] Budgeted prefetch controller implementation and internal API glue. - [x] Warmup profile definitions and proto-to-config mappers. - [x] Compact quant bundle schema, packer/unpacker, and registry upload flow. - [x] econ-init CLI with trace/dry-run input modes and dry-run report. - [x] Unit tests for prefetch decision logic and quant bundle verifier. - [x] Integration test: simulated tenant arriving pattern -> warmup applied -> cold miss rate reduction validated. - [x] Documentation: console UI knobs, CLI usage, and release notes. Backcompat & safety: Default behavior is opt-in for tenants under trial tier; enterprise tenants can enable via tenant policy. A runtime feature flag (prefetch.v2) gates rollout; the controller falls back to legacy prefill when disabled. Related: builds on work from ENG-2160 (hot-path prefill) and reuses parts of the sample-synth framework. Migration path: - Existing prefill configs are translated on upgrade using a migration script included in this PR. - Bundles uploaded to registry will not be used until tenant opts-in or admin toggles rollout. Monitoring: added new metrics: prefetch.budget_spent, prefetch.seed_coverage, quant.bundle_match_rate, econ-cli.dryrun_delta. Rolling plan: staged rollout to 10% of tenants for 48h, observe cold-miss and tail-latency signals, then expand.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Overall 👍. Two questions: 1) How does the controller avoid thundering-prefetch when a tenant crosses the threshold? 2) Have you measured the additional memory overhead for storing qbundles in registry?

Maya Chen (author): For 1) controller enforces soft ramping + randomized staggered prefill windows; details in controller docstring and integration test sim. For 2) qbundles are compact (avg 1.6MB per model) and stored in compressed blobs; added metrics and a hard cap per-tenant registry quota.
Lucia Gomez: Need a follow-up: add e2e test against Dedicated nodes with limited GPU memory — prefetch behavior interacts with shard placement. Can we add a smoke test?
Maya Chen: Added integration test and opened follow-up task ENG-2215 to broaden Dedicated-node e2e coverage.
ci_checks: e2e: queued -> rerun required (flaky), passed on rerun
merge_outcome_summary: Merged after two rounds of review. CI green after rerun of flaky e2e. Migration script included. Feature gated behind runtime flag for safe rollout.
release_notes: Introduce budgeted coldstart prefetch controller, tenant warmup profiles, compact quant bundles (.qbundle) and econ-init CLI. Default opt-in behavior for non-enterprise tenants. Monitor prefetch.* and quant.* metrics. See docs for rollout instructions.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature via runtime flag prefetch.v2. Apply migration script during maintenance window. Watch metrics prefetch.budget_spent and prefetch.seed_coverage for first 48h of rollout. If budget burn is high, reduce tenant default budget via central policy.
risk_assessment: Medium. Prefetch reduces cold misses but can increase short-term load if misconfigured. Mitigations: feature flag, budget caps, conservative defaults, staged rollout and telemetry alerting.
